points.what: EMEA orders rose 23.0% WoW to 171, contributing 37.6% of the week's total order increase, more than any other region.
points.so_what: Order growth this week did not come mainly from APAC, the largest region by share, since EMEA was the leading contributor to the increase.

points.what: Search orders rose 12.2% WoW to 578, contributing 74.1% of the week's total order increase.
points.so_what: With Search already the dominant channel at 69.8% of orders, this week's growth further concentrated order volume in a single channel.

points.what: Organic orders rose 25.0% WoW to 130, contributing 30.6% of the week's order increase, the second-largest driver after Search.
points.so_what: Facebook fell 6.8% WoW and contributed negatively to the change, meaning smaller channels also declined while growth concentrated in the two largest channels.

points.what: AOV fell 4.6% WoW and 12.4% YoY to $82.16.
points.so_what: Revenue's 6.0% WoW growth came from more orders (up 11.4% WoW) rather than bigger baskets, since AOV fell over the same week.

points.what: Cancellation rate rose 0.2pp WoW to 12.9%, but is down 1.2pp YoY.
points.so_what: The WoW increase is a step in the wrong direction even though the rate remains below last year's level, so this is a trend worth monitoring rather than a one-off.

points.what: The 14-Day Return Rate for the week of 23 Feb 2026 was 9.7%, up 0.7pp WoW and 1.0pp YoY.
points.so_what: Both comparisons point the same bad direction, adding to signs that order quality is softening alongside this week's order growth.

points.what: New signups were flat WoW at 260, and up just 1.6% YoY.
points.so_what: Orders grew 11.4% WoW and 51.9% YoY over the same periods, so new customer growth is running far behind order growth on both measures.

summary.headline: Mixed week: revenue beat target while orders fell short, and the quarter remains behind target with two weeks left in Q1.

points.what: Orders rose 11.4% WoW and 51.9% YoY to 828.
points.so_what: The week still finished at 94.6% of target, a gap of 47 orders.

points.what: Revenue rose 6.0% WoW and 35.0% YoY to $59,238, a level outside its recent 8-week range.
points.so_what: At 104.8% of target, revenue was the only KPI ahead this week, offsetting part of the quarter's shortfall.

points.what: QTD and YTD revenue are both at 93.1% of target, with 2 weeks left in the quarter.
points.so_what: The quarter's remaining target of $172,424 must be covered in the final 2 weeks, well above this week's $59,238 in revenue.

points.what: Orders reached 828 against a target of 875, or 94.6% of target.
points.so_what: The 47-order gap needs to be closed against a next-week target of 817.

points.what: Revenue reached $59,238 against a target of $56,550, or 104.8% of target.
points.so_what: This is the only KPI ahead of target this week, and next week's target rises to $59,654.

points.what: QTD and YTD revenue attainment are both 93.1% of target, with a $44,764 gap to date.
points.so_what: The required weekly run-rate for the rest of the year is $78,254, well above the recent 8-week run-rate of $54,350, so the current pace would not close the full-year gap of $3,286,671.

points.what: The cancellation rate rose 0.2pp WoW to 12.9%.
points.so_what: At $680 of revenue per cancellation point, this WoW rise works against a quarter that is already $44,764 behind target.

points.what: The 14-Day Return Rate for the week of 23 Feb 2026 rose to 9.7%, up 0.7pp WoW and up 1.0pp YoY.
points.so_what: Rising on both a WoW and YoY basis marks this as a deteriorating trend in order quality to watch.

points.what: QTD revenue is at 93.1% of target, with $172,424 still needed in the final 2 weeks of the quarter.
points.so_what: The required full-year weekly run-rate of $78,254 remains well above the current 8-week run-rate of $54,350, so the year is not on pace at current performance.
